## Verdict

**All prior guideline and code findings for this amendment scope are closed. Nothing blocks.** This covers the prospective XML and the code only. It does not approve gates 1024 or 1025, the source readings, schema validation, any PDF/HTML export, or production acceptance.

- **Model:** `claude-opus-5-5` (Opus 5.5). My effort setting isn't shown to me, so I can't confirm it was medium.
- **Hashes:** `/tmp/day2-close-final-amendment-review/manifest.json` is the binding hash list. I read all 21 files it lists (all of the QA/source JSON, the code, both prior reviews and the 11 XML files), but I can't compute hashes, so I'm relying on your post-read check that nothing changed.

## Encoding-v2 findings, now closed

| # | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Verse-end marks | The XML now uses ASCII `:` (for example HE `morning_ashrei.xml:52`, `barukh_adonai.xml:39`, `nishmat.xml:39`). The convention is recorded in `guideline_amendments.json:3`, and the raw `׃` readings are kept in the source review. |
| 2 | Missing closing quote at 103:1 | EN `nishmat.xml:39` has `<choice><sic>Name.</sic><corr>Name’.</corr></choice>`. This matches the earlier 35:10 quote on the same line (`…like Thee’.`), and the q80 reader (confidence 0.99) confirms the print omits the mark. |
| 3 | Leftover self-referencing source on 145:1 | It's gone. Only the superscription line has the verse milestone; the rest of verse 1 is plain text (HE `:54-55`, EN `:47-48`). |
| 4 | No attribution on the 150:6 repeat | Fixed: `psalm_150_repeat.xml:39` now has `seg/@source="…bible:psalms/150/6"`. |
| 5 | Header pointing only to the s25–s45 records | All three spines and every witness now point to `sources/marmorstein_rosh_hashanah_2/batches/`. |
| 6 | Why 144:15 is contextual | `hoshiah_et_ammekha.xml:39` already provides canonical `bible:psalms/144/15`. Its hash `d71d3750…` matches the manifest and the recipe's `protected_files`. So the contextual `prayer:ashrei/quoted_144_15` is correct. |
| 7 | Note type for the standing direction | Kept as `instruction`, and the reason is recorded. |

Two source amendments are also applied:
- `אֱלהִים` in Psalm 72:18 without the holam (`barukh_adonai.xml:39`).
- `כַּיָּם` with the dagesh in the kaf (HE `nishmat.xml:39`).

## Code

The only change from approved v6 is the edition-text assignment at `pesuqei_close.py:49-52`. It is a fixed string inside an `is not None` guard and doesn't affect any boundary, call, scope or guard logic, so the v6 approval still holds.

The five low/nit items from the v6 review were not addressed in this change. They don't block, but they are still open:
- The check for two new files crossing languages (HE `a.xml`, EN `b.xml` sharing one identity).
- A real dry run to confirm the Psalm 146/10 premise.
- The missing regression tests.
- `KeyError` instead of `ValueError` when an instruction lacks a required field.
- Checking `expanded_target` against `expanded_calls`.

## Remaining issues (low, record-keeping only)

1. **Two records disagree about the quote at scan 80.** `source_review_conditional.json` (note for scan 80, around line 968) says "do not supply a missing end quote", while the amendment supplies it through `corr`. The encoding is right, because `sic` keeps the printed reading. But add one line to the amendments saying the source instruction is met by keeping `sic`, and that `corr` is an editorial layer allowed by JLPTEI.
2. **The conditional source review is bound to old files.** It records `segmentation_proof.json` as `d36b01b4…`, but the current proof is `6e166295…`, and the readings hash moved from `27cb8661…` to `3b2472c8…`. The current chain is internally consistent: the recipe's `readings_sha256` equals the proof's `generated_readings_sha256`, and the recipe's `segmentation_proof_sha256` equals the manifest. The final `source_approval.json` and `recipe_approval.json` need to bind these current hashes. `main()` already enforces this, since `source_approval_sha256` is `null` and nothing can be written until then.

## Still not approved

- **Gate 1024:** the mark after `בָּרְכִי`, scan 80. The XML currently has no mark there.
- **Gate 1025:** the mark on `וְכָרוֹת֙`, scan 72. The XML currently encodes a pashta.
- Any PDF/HTML or production acceptance.
